title: Francis and the sultan (1219)
hook: in the middle of a crusade Francis crosses the lines to talk with Sultan al-Kamil

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Crusades, told honestly. Your line was tell it honestly. Today, one man walks out of that hard story.

Outside the Egyptian city of Damietta, two armies face each other: a crusader army, camped and waiting, and the sultan's army across the way. Between them is ground nobody crosses unless they mean to fight. A man in a rough habit walks out into it anyway, with one companion and no weapon. He isn't carrying a message from the generals. He wants to talk to the sultan himself. His name is Francis.
screen: `TWO ARMIES AT DAMIETTA.` → `GROUND NOBODY CROSSES.` → `A MAN IN A ROUGH HABIT.`

segments.voice: A bishop in the crusader camp, Jacques de Vitry, wrote about it. Francis, he says, went over to the sultan's side unarmed. Soldiers seized him on the road; he told them he was a Christian and asked to be taken to their lord. The sultan, al-Kamil, received him. Jacques writes that the sultan listened to Francis preach for some days, then had him taken back safely to the Christian camp, and asked him to pray for him. A later life of Francis, by Bonaventure, adds more: that Francis offered to walk through fire to show his faith, and the sultan declined; that the sultan offered him rich gifts, and Francis refused them. These come later, and some readers take them as legend. What the eyewitness gives is simpler: two men on opposite sides of a war, and a conversation. In a rule he wrote for his brothers, Francis tells those who go among Muslims there are two ways to live. One is to preach, when they see it pleases God. The other, which he puts first, is not to argue or quarrel, but to be subject to every human creature for God's sake. That's a line from the first letter of Peter, in the Douay-Rheims: "Be ye subject therefore to every human creature for God's sake." Francis didn't end the war. He walked through it, across the lines.
screen: `UNARMED INTO THE SULTAN'S CAMP.` · `THE SULTAN HEARS HIM.` · `LATER STORIES OF FIRE AND GIFTS.` · `FIRST, DO NOT QUARREL.` · then, large: `ACROSS THE LINES.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person across a line from you: politics, a family quarrel, a different faith. Hold their face, not their side, and look for one question you'd ask if you only wanted to understand them. If you pray, hold them before God for a breath or two.
Francis. In the middle of a crusade, he crossed the lines unarmed, and Sultan al-Kamil received him and heard him out. Today's word.
Your line: across the lines. Next, we go back to where Francis started. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Franciscans remember the meeting at Damietta as part of their calling, and Catholic and Muslim groups sometimes recall it when they meet for dialogue; Franciscan friars still serve at holy sites in the Holy Land.

chat.says: Did Saint Francis really walk into an enemy camp in the middle of a war?
options: An eyewitness says he went unarmed, the sultan heard him, and sent him back safely.
Yes, but he went with soldiers, to demand that the sultan surrender the city.
No, that's a legend; nobody at the time ever wrote a word about it.
